title: Taking turns to choose the weekend plan
description: One family, four Saturdays, four different ideas of fun. A simple rota — this week you choose, next week I do — ends the weekend negotiation and quietly teaches everyone to plan for others.

body.heading: The rota ends the argument
paragraphs: Weekend plans fail in the choosing, not the doing: the loudest voice wins, or nobody decides and Saturday evaporates. A choosing rota replaces the contest with a calendar. When it is your turn, you choose — within the household's real limits of time and money — and everyone else's job is to come along in good faith.
Knowing your turn is coming changes how you spend other people's turns. You attend their museum or their match the way you hope they will attend yours.

body.heading: Plan for your audience
paragraphs: The advanced version is the real lesson: when your turn comes, choose something you love that you also think the others might enjoy, and say why you picked it. Choosing-for-others is a skill adults use constantly — in gifts, in work, in hosting — and the weekend rota is a gentle place to learn it.
Keep a list of past choices on the fridge. Patterns appear quickly: who always picks food, who never picks outdoors — and the list itself becomes a small family history.

takeaway: Rotate who chooses the weekend plan, attend each other's choices in good faith, and learn to plan with your audience in mind.
